notes: Three spec candidates per view (cap). Every --check run on a distinct spec is one attempt; the raw check output of each attempt is preserved in attempts/<spec>.check.txt. Re-running --check on an already-counted spec (the evidence harness does this) is not a new candidate.

attempts.note: Orientation probe: cp->pgrpc->q and web->wapi->q intake, auto tb layout, full verb labels. Result: extent 52x24, 0 detours, 4/4 labels, 1 ambiguous owner (the two routes into the River queue bend toward each other and their heads land 2 cells apart).

Explicit-layers probe ([web,cp],[wapi,pgrpc],[],[q]) to buy vertical room for the two labels. Result: explicit packing shrank the canvas to 36 cells wide, so the 22-char label had no clear cell (1 skipped) and 1 ambiguous owner remained. Rejected.

Final: same auto layout, verbs abbreviated (terminate->term, reprovision->reprov) to reduce label span. Result: 4/4 labels, 0 detours, 0 skipped, 1 ambiguous owner (reinstall/reprov, whose left edge sits nearer the sibling route's bend than its own head). Chosen as best of three.

Auto tb layout of the provisioning chain plus the mch<->boot pair and mch->s3. Result: extent 65x40, 1 bridge, 2 ambiguous owners (iPXE request and pull boot image both sat beside the two adjacent corridors leaving the machine box). Rejected.

Explicit layers with an empty band between the machine layer and the boot layer to lengthen the pair. Result: extent 44x47, taller than the 46-row drawing area, so the app reported overflow; the 20-char label had no free slot and 1 ambiguous owner remained. Rejected.

Final: single-row last layer with reserved slots ([boot,"",s3]) so the boot server is staggered away from the machine box and the machine's two outgoing corridors are no longer adjacent. Result: extent 65x38, 0 crossings, 6/6 labels, 0 detours, 1 shortened route, 1 ambiguous owner (boot.ipxe + S3 args sits between two parallel runs). Chosen.

All four Postgres writers spread in one layer above a tall empty band. Result: 0 ambiguous owners and 7/7 labels, but extent 85x41 exceeds the 77-column pane, so the graph would have to be panned. 6 bridges. Rejected on fit.
Reconcile loop lifted to the agent layer to shrink the widest row to three slots. Result: extent 68x42 (fits), 2 bridges, 7/7 labels, 1 ambiguous owner.

Final: queue lifted next to the agent, so the writer row carries three slots and the queue route reaches Postgres from a different height. Result: extent 66x41, 1 bridge, 7/7 labels, 0 detours, 1 forced route, 1 ambiguous owner. Chosen (fewer bridges than a2, fits the pane).
Queue fan above a tall empty band, three targets in one row. Result: extent 62x39, 0 bridges, 6/6 labels, 2 ambiguous owners (two 16-20 char labels landed on the adjacent queue corridors).
Staircase: each queue target in its own layer so the jogs would land at different heights. Result: extent 41x47, taller than the drawing area (overflow) and 3 ambiguous owners. Rejected.

Final: queue centred so its three fan routes leave by three different borders (left, bottom, right); targets staggered across slots. Result: extent 77x39 (fits at 100%), 0 bridges, 6/6 labels, 0 detours, 1 ambiguous owner (diagnose uploads landed on the neighbouring left-border run). Chosen.
